chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated to us from Muhammad ibn al-Fadl, from 'Udhafir, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say: 'Verily, Allah chose Islam for Himself as a religion, so be its virtuous companions through generosity and good character.'
ai.seo_question: How should Muslims behave to honor Islam as Allah's chosen religion?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Kitab al-Zuhd*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) links the theological acceptance of Islam by Allah to the ethical conduct of its adherents, emphasizing that generosity and noble character are the practical manifestations of this divine favor. This reflects the Shia emphasis on *akhlaq* (character) as an integral component of faith, where internal belief is validated through external social virtues like *sakhā'* (generosity). The narration underscores that being a 'good companion' to Islam requires active moral engagement rather than mere ritual observance.
